elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 18.3 is retained unchanged: "shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, United States, without reference to conflict of law principles." New York is the preferred governing law and required no edit.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: New Section 17.3(a): "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, USA shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any Dispute, and each Party irrevocably submits to that jurisdiction; provided that either Party may apply to any other court of competent jurisdiction for temporary injunctive relief." The only other-court carve-out is the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, which preserves the exclusive merits forum. The residual arbitration machinery (including the Osaka seat mechanic in the former 17.3(a) and the tribunal powers in 17.3(g)) is expressly switched off by "The remaining provisions of this Section 17.3, other than Section 17.3(f), shall not apply," so no contradictory mandatory-arbitration forum survives. The pre-existing Section 17.2 Expert and inventorship carve-outs are subject-matter exclusions that existed before the redline and were correctly left untouched.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 18.3 continues to specify the laws of the State of New York; no Delaware, California, or England and Wales law is selected. This is expected because the drafter targeted the preferred level, which is superior for us.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The forum is set to the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Again expected, as the redline targets the preferred position.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York law was already in place under Section 18.3 and required no edit, and the new Section 17.3(a) supplies exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction over the merits with only a temporary injunctive relief carve-out.

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original Section 17.3 imposed mandatory ICC arbitration that Array could seat in Osaka, Japan, which is walk-away territory under GOVLAW, and no court forum for the merits existed anywhere in the Agreement (17.3(g) preserved court access only for provisional relief).

Minimal: the edit changes only the forum mechanic (heading, the "final and binding arbitration" operative words, and the seat provision in 17.3(a)) and leaves Section 18.3, the Section 17.2 Expert track, the inventorship carve-out, and the Section 17.3(f) internal-counsel privilege protection intact. The disapplication sentence is necessary rather than an unnecessary override, because subsections 17.3(b)-(g) would otherwise survive as contradictory arbitration machinery; a bare jurisdiction sentence would not do the job here.

Intent preserved: allocation of Expert-determinable matters, the inventorship remedies carve-out, and each Party's access to provisional relief all survive without contradiction, and the disapplication sentence resolves the conflict with the retained arbitration text.

Cleanup recommendation (not a level failure): the replaced Section 17.3(a) contained the definitions of "Arbitration Tribunal" and "Rules", which are still used in the retained-but-disapplied Section 17.3(g) and possibly in the retained Section 17.3(f). Because 17.3(g) is expressly inoperative this creates no operative ambiguity, but the cleaner execution is to strike Sections 17.3(b)-(e) and (g) outright (keeping (f)) rather than leaving disapplied text with orphaned defined terms, and to confirm no other Section of the Agreement cross-refers to "arbitration", the "Arbitration Tribunal", or the "Rules".
Fallback is not met by design; no repair is required since the higher preferred level is fully achieved.
